answer: A concrete defense is a bridge toll paid in proof: to cross from unknown to trusted, each identity burns an ember of 0.05 GPU-hours solving a fresh puzzle chained to the previous epoch's hash. The chain's delta rule rejects any two crossings whose puzzle answers share a solution prefix, so cloned identities cannot amortize one solve across many keys. Every crossing is priced and logged, and an attacker holding k identities pays k embers per epoch with no way to reset or parallelize the chain, keeping marginal cost linear in n.
